transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-15 15:00 PST
Duration: ~78 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Daniel (BrightScale CTO), Maya (Platform), Jorge (Security), Samir (Infra), Rita (Procurement)

Summary: Deep technical session focused on on-prem / air-gapped deployment concerns: artifact delivery process, offline licensing for GPU drivers, driver packaging and compatibility, KV cache behavior, batching strategies, quantization tradeoffs and expected latency/throughput. Customer has strict controls (air-gap, limited outbound, procurement windows).

Topics: artifact delivery, offline licensing & driver activation, GPU driver offline install, KV cache persistence and warmup, batching & latency SLOs, quantization profiles and quality regression, network/VPC constraints, audit/logging requirements.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making the time. i think we have about an hour 15 today, we'll get into the deep tech details, priya will drive most of the infra bits.
[00:18] Priya: hi all, quick agenda -- artifact delivery approach for air-gapped sites, offline licensing & driver licensing flow, runtime perf (kv cache + batching), quantization impact and then q&a on security/logs. sound good?
[00:30] Daniel: yes that's perfect. just to set expectations, we're looking to run 4 racks initially, nvidia a100-ish hardware, fully airgapped, no external internet from the inference clusters. security will have to approve any usb/exchange process.
[00:45] Priya: got it. that's the common case we handle. two main delivery patterns: sealed artifact bundle (scp via approved jumpbox or physical transfer) or internal artifact repo seeded by ops. for air-gap we provide sha256-signed tarballs and a delivery checklist.
[01:05] Samir: when you say signed tarballs, do we need a specific cert chain? our org requires the bits to be verifiable by our hsm.
[01:12] Alex: good question — we support signing with a customer-provided gpg or we can sign and provide a separate verification manifest; for highest assurance you can sign the bundle on your side, or we provide signatures that you can verify against the manifest we publish to the secure portal. we can adapt to your HSM process.
[01:28] Maya: how big are these artifacts typically? models aside — just the runtime + drivers?
[01:33] Priya: runtime image + CUDA/NVIDIA driver packages + management agents ~ 1.2 to 8GB depending on driver+cuda combos. model weights are separate and big; they follow your model onboarding SOP.
[01:44] Jorge: security note — we need to see the delivery checklist before procurement; any scripts that run during install have to be auditable and we need verification of checksums.
[01:52] Alex: absolutely, we'll share the checklist and the install scripts with comments.
[01:55] Priya: switching to licensing — offline licensing for GPU drivers: some NIC vendors use offline keys; with NVIDIA driver OEM there's an offline activation token we can include in the bundle. Redwood supports an offline license daemon that validates the license locally against a signed token; no outbound call required.
[02:16] Daniel: okay so runtime will start with a license token in the bundle and the daemon validates locally? what about renewals or expirations?
[02:24] Priya: token-based with time windows; renewals typically done via periodic physical re-seed or secure pull from an approved proxy when policy allows. we also support long-lived perpetual tokens for customers with strict windows, subject to procurement/legal.
[02:37] Samir: procurement will push back on per-seat licensing; how granular is that? per instance, per GPU?
[02:42] Alex: licensing is flexible — we can map to instances or GPU counts. we'll surface options in the licensing doc we'll share.
[02:49] Priya: now runtime perf. our serving runtime has continuous batching and KV cache; the KV cache persists across sessions if you enable on-disk caching for warm start.
[03:00] Maya: curious about KV cache persistence — if a node reboots, how long before warm state is effective? is it just disk-backed or do you support a replicated KV?
[03:09] Priya: disk-backed by default; warmup time depends on model and sequence distribution. for large models, cold-to-warm can be tens of seconds to a few minutes depending on cache hit rate and the throughput of your disks. we also support a pre-warm snapshot you can seed during deploy — that's common for airgap installs.
[03:28] Daniel: pre-warm snapshot sounds useful. is that an exported KV file we ship?
[03:32] Priya: yes, exactly; we produce an exported KV snapshot (sharded per GPU) that you can apply during install. warning: snapshots are model-version specific.
[03:39] Jorge: from an audit perspective, does the KV snapshot contain any PII or sensitive tokens?
[03:45] Priya: snapshot contains KV tokens that are model context; we recommend stripping any customer-sensitive info before snapshot creation; we can also encrypt the snapshot with customer KMS keys.
[03:55] Samir: performance numbers — what latency/throughput should we expect for 2048 context, 1 request per second per client, batching to 16?
[04:05] Priya: rough numbers on A100 80GB: with batching of 16 and kv-hit rate ~60%, we see p95 generation latency ~220-320ms per request for common LLMs (7B-ish to 13B fp16); heavier models or longer decode steps increase that. throughput depends on tokenization and token/sec — per-GPU throughput for 13B fp16 about 120-180 tokens/sec when fully utilized.
[04:28] Daniel: can you clarify fp16 vs int8 quantized performance?
[04:32] Priya: yes — fp16 runs faster on full precision paths with tensor cores; int8 quantized (we do 8-bit PTQ/LUT) reduces memory and can increase throughput 1.3x-2x depending on kernel support, at cost of some quality delta. we also support GPTQ-style and newer quant schemes; results vary by model.
[04:50] Maya: how do you handle kernel selection offline? we don't allow node to phone-home for optimized kernel downloads.
[04:56] Priya: good point. runtime ships with a catalog of kernels for common architectures; if you want additional vendor kernels we can include them in the artifact bundle. we also include a kernel selector that runs a local micro-benchmark on first boot and picks the best path; all artifacts are signed.
[05:13] Samir: what about the nvidia driver compatibility matrix? our infra team is strict about driver versions.
[05:19] Priya: we maintain a compatibility matrix (we'll send it) — runtime expects certain CUDA+driver combos. for airgap we provide both the tested NVIDIA driver tar and the patched install scripts for your airgap SOP. note: some cloud-optimized drivers have telemetry; we provide OSS drivers or vendor-official bundles with telemetry disabled where possible.
[05:40] Jorge: telemetry must be fully verifiable and disabled by default. also audit logs of install actions must be stored centrally and immutable.
[05:46] Alex: we support storing install logs locally and shipping them to your internal logging endpoint when allowed; for airgap they can be collected via the same sealed transfer method.
[05:55] Priya: moving back to KV caching and batching strategies — the serving runtime can do dynamic batching or fixed-window batching. dynamic batching tries to minimize added latency but will respect per-request latency limits.
[06:08] Daniel: what's the policy for latency SLOs? we need p95 under 500ms for interactive features.
[06:13] Priya: with properly tuned batching (max batch 16, target latency 150-200ms), we can hit p95 under 500ms for 7B-13B ranges on A100 when KV-hit is decent. for larger models or heavy generation you should consider smaller batch sizes or dedicated capacity.
[06:29] Maya: are batching and KV cache configuration exposed in the UI/console or only via config files?
[06:34] Alex: in private deployments you get the same Console surface — config, metrics, per-route tuning — but in fully airgapped installs the Console runs inside your VPC; for the first install we provide a local WebUI you can access through your management network. configs are YAML and editable.
[06:49] Jorge: encryption of config at rest? keys?
[06:51] Priya: configs are encrypted at rest; we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key material, and we support storing secrets in your vault.
[06:58] Samir: can you explain how batching interacts with KV-caching for repeated requests? if we batch several requests that share prefixes, do you dedupe KV work?
[07:07] Priya: yes, we have prefix dedupe and shared KV lookup optimization — if requests share prefix tokens the runtime reuses cached keys rather than recompute. batching layer also supports prefix-grouping to reduce redundant compute.
[07:19] Daniel: what's the RBAC story on the private console and for the offline install assets? we have separate teams for infra and security.
[07:25] Alex: RBAC is plumbed through SSO/SAML in standard installs; for airgapped we integrate with your internal IdP (SAML) or local LDAP. role mappings are configurable.
[07:34] Maya: can we lock down who can run installs or apply KV snapshots?
[07:37] Priya: yes, install operations require a role with permission and every action is recorded in the local audit log.
[07:43] Jorge: for compliance we need access to tamper-evident logs — can those be HMAC'd and sealed?
[07:49] Priya: we support log signing as part of the bundle; we can HMAC logs with a customer key or sign them for extra assurance.
[07:58] Samir: about quantization — you mentioned quality regressions. how do you measure and baseline QA before rolling?
[08:05] Priya: we use a set of eval prompts (you can provide your own) and run automated quality regressions; Redwood Optimize provides delta scoring and fallback policies to revert to fp16 if quantized model drops below a threshold. we also support canary routing per model version.
[08:20] Daniel: will the quantized kernels be included in the offline bundle?
[08:24] Priya: yes, quantized kernels and model artifacts can be bundled. note: some quant schemes require custom kernels that we include and sign.
[08:33] Maya: on storage requirements — if we enable persistent KV for snapshots, what's disk footprint?
[08:38] Priya: depends on your workload; typical KV for mid-size models might be a few GBs per shard. we provide estimates after you share the sample prompt distribution; the perf spreadsheet will model that.
[08:51] Rita: procurement quick question — what's the lead time for getting an offline license token?
[08:55] Alex: normally 3-5 business days once the procurement PO is validated; for perpetual tokens we can extend that but procurement/legal need to sign specific terms.
[09:04] Jorge: any known gotchas with airgap installs and GPU driver signatures? we've had problems with vendor driver installers that require network during package install.
[09:11] Priya: yes some vendor installers try to fetch telemetry or driver checks; we vendor a pre-extracted driver packaging that contains the necessary binaries for offline install and patched install scripts. we test those on our reference airgap lab.
[09:25] Samir: for the pre-warm snapshot, if model is updated, do we need a new snapshot per model version?
[09:29] Priya: yes, snapshots are model-version tied. we recommend a snapshot per major version; minor tokenizer changes can also affect cache validity.
[09:38] Daniel: operationally, during a deploy we'll likely want a canary for a subset of traffic. can we route traffic internally without internet access?
[09:45] Priya: yes the routing is internal to your VPC, canary config is local. metrics and tracing hooks point to your internal telemetry endpoints; nothing needs to egress.
[09:54] Maya: about tracing, does the default runtime emit OpenTelemetry traces?
[09:57] Priya: it emits OTEL spans that you can export to your collector; for airgapped installs the collector runs locally and you can push ATA later via sealed transfer if required.
[10:06] Jorge: security again — we need to ensure keys used for signing are not shipped.
[10:10] Alex: we never ship Redwood private signing keys; we recommend you use your own key pair or verify against our published manifest.
[10:18] Priya: a few more perf specifics: if you enable on-disk KV and also pre-warm, typical steady-state p95 reduces by 30-50% compared to cold start, depending on hit rate. batching increases throughput but increases median latency by a small amount; dynamic batching aims to balance that.
[10:35] Samir: do you have benchmark artifacts we can run on our infra? raw runner script?
[10:39] Alex: yes we'll share a lightweight benchmark harness you can run locally (python script + sample prompts + expected metrics). we'll include instructions for airgap run.
[10:47] Priya: also including kernel microbenchmarks to pick best kernel paths per GPU.
[10:52] Maya: on the quantization regression detection — can you show us how the Optimize UI surfaces delta scoring?
[10:57] Alex: we can demo that in a follow-up demo; for today we'll send screenshots and the perf sheet.
[11:02] Daniel: what about fallback policies — if quantized variant drops below threshold do you auto-fallback to fp16?
[11:07] Priya: yes, we support automatic rollback to a fallback variant and automatic routing to fallback model variant at inference-time with minimal disruption.
[11:14] Jorge: legal will want the exact language on data retention and where logs are stored.
[11:18] Alex: we'll include the retention defaults and options; you can configure retention on the local console and we can provide a compliant retention export.
[11:26] Samir: any special kernel requirements for multi-GPU NVLINK performance?
[11:30] Priya: the runtime is NUMA-aware and supports NVLINK for model sharding. we ship NCCL and tuned parameters for inter-GPU comms in the artifact bundle. those are pre-configured for topologies, but you can override.
[11:42] Daniel: does the runtime require a control plane connection to Redwood for license verification or rollout control?
[11:48] Priya: no, for private airgapped installs you run the control plane locally; the Redwood control plane is optional for hosted customers. license verification can be purely local using signed tokens.
[11:58] Maya: what about future kernel updates — will we need to re-sign and re-validate?
[12:02] Priya: yes kernel or driver updates are new artifacts; you'll get a new signed bundle to apply. we recommend a staging apply before prod.
[12:10] Alex: open floor for detailed questions — Jorge?
[12:12] Jorge: one more: can we get cryptographic proof-of-installation? like signed attestations?
[12:18] Priya: we can incorporate a signed attestation blob post-install that includes checksums of installed files, timestamps, and an HMAC with your key. that can be stored in your artifact repo.
[12:29] Samir: good. last infra detail: network windows — we have scheduled maintenance windows where outbound is allowed for short pulls. can you support a pull-based renewal?
[12:38] Alex: yes we support pull from an approved proxy; the renewal flow can be configured to only accept proxy pull from an allowlisted IP/range.
[12:45] Daniel: ok that covers most. huge thanks — next steps please?
[12:50] Alex: recap of next steps — i'll send the offline licensing guide and the driver checklist, priya will seed the perf spreadsheet and kernel microbenchmarks, we'll propose install week. and we'll include SOC2 and network diagrams for Jorge.
[13:05] Priya: we'll also include example config YAMLs for batching/kv and sample scripts for snapshot export and apply.
[13:12] Rita: procurement will expect the lead times in writing, please include standard SLA and kick-off steps.
[13:18] Alex: will do. any final quick q's?
[13:22] Daniel: none from me, thanks.
[13:24] Maya: no thanks, this was helpful.
[13:26] Jorge: good session.
[13:28] Samir: thanks.

End notes: deliverables to be shared as action items. cadence: follow-on demo for Optimize UI + canary routing, and scheduled install window.
